title: Test-optional Policies: Overcoming Strategic Behavior and Informational Gaps
source_inventory_policy: Source basis: /tmp/econcs_source_text/LG21TestOptionalPolicies.txt and paper-local SOURCE_AUDIT.md. Curated by the 2026-06-28 source-grounded coverage pass. Dashboard-seeded keys were checked against the source inventory reports/source text when available; explicitly missing named source items are recorded as out_of_scope rather than silently omitted.

definition1_source_equilibrium.statement: A source equilibrium consists of feasible access decisions, best-response utility maximization among feasible actions in every student information state, and estimation consistency.

definition2_latent_skill_fair.statement: A policy surface is latent-skill fair when, in every equilibrium, applicants with the same latent skill and base group receive the same estimate law whether or not they have access.

definition3_observable_fair.statement: A policy surface is observably fair when, in every equilibrium and base group, the access and no-access observable estimate laws are equal.

definition4_demographic_fair.statement: A policy surface is demographically fair when, in every equilibrium, the demographic access and no-access estimate laws are equal.

definition5_test_blank.statement: A policy surface is test-blank when, in every equilibrium, base group, and test value, the base-only estimate equals the full-feature estimate.

theorem3_1_optional_reporting.statement: In the hidden-access optional-reporting source model, when access fractions are below one, every source equilibrium has strategic withholding: everyone takes the test, some base-score pair is not reported, reporting is cutoff-shaped within each base group, and the base-mixed Gaussian posterior-law surface is not latent-skill fair, not observable fair, and not demographic fair.

theorem3_1_report_required.statement: In the hidden-access report-required source model with positive slopes and access fractions below one, every source equilibrium has strategic withholding: some base-skill pair does not take the test, taking is cutoff-shaped within each base group, and the base-mixed affine-skill posterior-law surface is not latent-skill fair, not observable fair, and not demographic fair.

theorem3_2_optional_reporting_fairness_i.statement: In the optional-reporting source model, under source-equilibrium, threshold-reporting, and the no-reporter-to-test-blank normalization, latent-skill fairness or observable fairness of the event-share binary-mixture surface implies test-blankness.

theorem3_2_optional_reporting_no_test_re.statement: Under the same optional-reporting hypotheses, if the event-share binary-mixture surface is latent-skill fair or observable fair, then there is no base/test triple where the base-only and full-feature estimates differ.

theorem3_2_report_required_fairness_impo.statement: In the report-required source model, under source-equilibrium, threshold-taking, and the no-taker-to-test-blank normalization, latent-skill fairness or observable fairness of the event-share binary-mixture surface implies test-blankness.

theorem3_2_report_required_no_test_relev.statement: Under the same report-required hypotheses, if the event-share binary-mixture surface is latent-skill fair or observable fair, then there is no base/test triple where the base-only and full-feature estimates differ.

lemma4_1_observed_access_strategy_proofn.statement: With observed access and a positive test scale, the fully specified optional-reporting and report-required source equilibria choose take-and-report in every student information state, giving the strategy-proofness step.

proposition4_2_bayesian_access_estimates.statement: For the fully specified observed-access source equilibria, any positive-slope base-indexed one-test posterior-law surface chooses take-and-report in every information state and is not latent-skill fair.

proposition4_3_bayesian_optimal_not_obse.statement: For the fully specified observed-access source equilibria, any base-mixed extra-signal posterior-law surface with positive extra-noise variance chooses take-and-report in every information state and is not observable fair or demographic fair.

definition6_resampling_policy.statement: The resampling policy uses the resampling experiment's conditional signal-given-base kernel.

theorem4_4_resampling_policy.statement: For every resampling experiment, the fully specified observed-access source equilibria choose take-and-report in every information state, and the access-estimate and resampling-estimate kernels are observable fair and demographic fair with respect to the base profile.
